topic: Understanding Discrete Convolutions: From Filters to Features
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Engineering Students

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Sliding Window
lecture_lines: Imagine a magnifying glass scanning a photo.
[Asset: magnifying_glass_scan] We call this scan a filter.
[Asset: filter_sliding] It extracts local features like edges.
[Asset: edge_highlight] See how it highlights whiskers?
[Asset: whiskers_detail] This is the sliding window.
animations: Create a 5x5 grid in #FFFFFF, center screen.
Animate a 3x3 square boundary in #FF0000 sliding across the grid.
Highlight the 3x3 window's intersection with grid pixels.
Pulse the window boundary color to #FFFF00 for emphasis.
Draw a temporary green boundary [#00FF00] around the current window focus.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics: Multiply and Sum
lecture_lines: [Asset: multiply_step] Now sum the results together.
[Asset: sum_step] This value represents the center.
[Asset: result_pixel] Example: one times A plus D.
animations: Arrange input grid and filter matrix in adjacent grid positions.
Highlight corresponding pixel pairs with colored lines in #FFFF00.
Show transformation numbers multiplying in floating text.
Sum the products and display the result in #00FFFF.
Transition the summation formula into the output grid.

sections.title: Visualizing Filters: Edge Detection
lecture_lines: [Asset: kernel_variety] Sobel filters detect sharp contrast.
[Asset: sobel_edge] See blurred images become sharp.
animations: Display a grayscale square mobject in #FFFFFF.
Overlay a vertical gradient matrix to highlight edges.
Transform image colors to show high-contrast edges in #FF8000.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Heart of Neural Networks
lecture_lines: [Asset: cnn_layer] Machines learn optimal filter weights.
animations: Render a series of circles representing neural network layers.
Animate arrows moving from filter outputs to the next layer of nodes.
Flash active nodes with a #FF00FF glow effect.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
